recon.notes: Squarespace, static: each of the parser's two urls IS one listing — a single announcement block rewritten per party (the home page for the San Francisco edition, /brooklyn for the New York edition). Neither page prints a year: "SATURDAY, SEPT 26" matches 2026-09-26 (a Saturday, the eve of Folsom Street Fair 2026 — what "FOLSOM" refers to) and "SATURDAY SEPTEMBER 19" matches 2026-09-19 (a Saturday, the recon date itself, so the Brooklyn party is the night of the read). The ra.co and DICE ticket pages would settle year, door time and price but were not opened (no network on the recon date). Neither page states a recurrence for the party itself.

coverage.basis: One event per door. Home-page door (https://gruntparty.monster/, fetched 2026-09-19): exactly one announced party, Folsom Saturday Sept 26 at The Stud with one ra.co ticket link. Brooklyn door (https://gruntparty.monster/brooklyn, fetched 2026-09-19): exactly one announced party, Saturday September 19 at C'mon Everybody with one DICE ticket link. Published = 2 singles; both pages are overwritten per party, so no past listings exist. Confidence is medium rather than high because neither page prints a year and the ticket pages that would confirm it were not opened.

traps.label: "BROOKLYN" in the header nav (href="/brooklyn") on the home page, and "FOLSOM" (href="/") on /brooklyn
traps.why: Each page's header nav links to the other edition's page; the nav item carries no date, venue or ticket link, so it is not an event on the page it appears on. Each party is documented from its own page only — the Brooklyn night from /brooklyn, the Folsom night from / — never from the cross-link.
traps.note: The nav is rendered three times in each page's source (desktop, mobile, and the mobile overlay), so a text-window reader sees "FOLSOM | BROOKLYN" three times before the announcement. Since both urls are in the parser's config, a run should yield exactly one record per page, not a Folsom ghost from /brooklyn or vice versa.

openQuestions.q: Neither page prints a year. 2026 is inferred from the weekday match (Sept 26 and September 19 are both Saturdays in 2026) and from the Folsom Street Fair context; the ra.co (2447663) and DICE (j1e6d0b77886) ticket pages were not opened and would confirm year, door time and price.

Should the event titles be "GRUNT FOLSOM" / "GRUNT BROOKLYN" (site name + the page's edition label) or just "GRUNT"? The pages print no event name beyond those words; the ticket listings' titles (unread) may settle it.
